summary: Reviewed chat_announcements.py, schema_ddl/chat_announcements.py and the diffs to announcements.py, groups.py, scheduler.py, flags, db.py and routes/group_announcements.py. Authorization: create still goes through the existing member/free-limit/content-filter path; post_to_chat is StrictBool and checked_post_flag fails closed (422) when the chat_announcements flag is off for the poster; nobody gains new rights (edit/delete/restore unchanged, broadcasts fire only after the manager's permission checks succeed). Emission is idempotent (unique partial index + ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING), requires the poster to still be a live group member, non-deleted, published, flag on, and the scheduler only looks back 1h (no backfill). Injection: all SQL parameterised; the only f-string SQL pieces are module constants (system_kind literal, fixed EXISTS clause). Read side: lines are scoped by group_id, joined to non-deleted published announcements, hidden for flag-off viewers, author_set (blocked/departed) rule still applies, and a line whose announcement cannot load is dropped rather than faked; card serialized per viewer via AnnouncementsManager. Live frames go only to author_set members with the flag on; neutral card carries only data any member can already read, sync frames carry ids and action only; best-effort sends never fail the write. system_kind/announcement_id are stripped from legacy shape except the allowed kinds. Logs carry ids and exception type names only; no secrets or content. Line text is a constant, so soft-deleted lines leak nothing via other readers (pins/replies). Not verified: the two tests needing port 55432 were not run (per instruction, cluster untouched). Low-severity notes, not blocking: broadcast_sync after delete/update runs even if no line exists (it returns early, no leak); consider confirming message_pins/replies do not let a user pin or reply to a soft-deleted announcement line (harmless content-wise).
